content:
Affine homogenization (#39431) will enable us to smoothly translate concepts between affine spaces and linear spaces, e.g.

  • Submodule and AffineSubspace
  • LinearMap and AffineMap
  • ...

We are already using this heavily in our polyhedral repository for translating between convex sets and convex cones, as well as polytopes and finitely generated cones. We are also currently running a workshop on this repository, and some tension arose what should be fundamental geometric objects on both sides of homogenization.

  • On the affine side there is a tendency to work with Set as the fundamental object and assume the predicate IsConvexSet on top when necessary.
  • On the linear side there is a tendency to work with PointedCone, which is the bundled object for convex cones.

Neither approach currently has an analogue on the other side:

  • there is no bundled convex set in affine space. There is #39205 for bundled ConvexSet, but some (including me) are not fully convinced this is a good idea right now.
  • there is no natural object on the linear side that is the homogenization of a general Set. The correct equivalent would be something like SubMulAction but with the additional property that it contains the origin. In our repository we introduce this object as SubMulAction₀. Perhaps a better name would be Cone.

In the repository we have both, homogenization translating between Set and SubMulAction₀, as well as ConvexSet and PointedCone.

The question for the fundamental object comes up whenever we introduce a new geometric concept like faces, tangent cones, interior, etc.

Question: In affine space, should we define a new concept on Set or (bundled) ConvexSet?

Sets seem too pathological for many of these notions, but this does not hurt when writing down the definition. Lemmas may assume IsConvexSet whenever necessary. On the other hand, we might later want these notions on certain well-behaved non-convex objects, so ConvexSet is too restrictive in the long run. Same question comes up in linear space, except that here we currently default to PointedCone which will be too restrictive in these scenarios. The alternative is to define everything on SubMulAction₀.

Here is a proposal and I would like to hear your opinion:

  • We introduce Cone to mathlib, which is SubMulAction with 0, and serves as the natural "homogeneous set" in linear space.
  • We define homogeneous geometric concepts on Cone instead of PointedCone, including the existing IsFaceOf and Face.
  • We do not introduce bundled ConvexSet in affine space for now, until a good reason comes up.

I don't have the whole picture here, but the reason PointedCone is bundled is because it's just an abbrev for Submodule {c : R // 0 ≤ c} E and we usually have bundled objects for subspaces. Can I think of a convex set as a "sub-affine-space"? If so I think it can be bundled as well.

I think the word Cone should be reserved for when you have some partial order on your ring, and then being a cone means being closed under scalar multiplication of nonnegative scalars. Using cone for a general SubMulAction₀ where smul can be anything might be confusing.

That is right! So perhaps we want to mirror the PointedCone setup and define

abbrev Cone (R M) := SubMulAction₀ R≥0 M

Actually one could replace SubMulAction₀ with SubMulAction in this case. Is there any reason left to introduce the former?

Justus Springer said:

Can I think of a convex set as a "sub-affine-space"? If so I think it can be bundled as well.

Indeed, convex sets are the subsets of ConvexSpace that have a natural convex space structure in themselves. They are like AffineSubspace in that regard.
Note that Submodule is defined as the union of AddSubmonoid M and SubMulAction R M. So basically you are now proposing to remove closedness under addition from the definition of a cone?

Martin Winter said:

Actually one could replace SubMulAction₀ with SubMulAction in this case. Is there any reason left to introduce the former?

I personally don't see a reason to introduce SubMulAction₀. I also think we both agree that the name PointedCone in mathlib is bad, and it should be called ConvexCone or just Cone. The distinction between cones with/without the origin seems very unnatural to me, so I would even be fine with dropping docs#ConvexCone in favor of docs#PointedCone.

Justus Springer said:

Note that Submodule is defined as the union of AddSubmonoid M and SubMulAction R M. So basically you are now proposing to remove closedness under addition from the definition of a cone?

I am not sure I understand. I do not propose changing any existing subtype definitions, just to add a cone-type that is not closed under addition.

Justus Springer said:

The distinction between cones with/without the origin seems very unnatural to me, so I would even be fine with dropping docs#ConvexCone in favor of docs#PointedCone.

Something like this has been on its way for a while, not sure about the status (@Artie Khovanov).

By the way, I think the current ConvexCone can also be expressed as Submodule R>0 M if really needed.

I guess my point is I would aim to reduce the number of things that go by the name "cone" instead of adding another one. And I don't yet understand the motivation of adding a cone type that's not closed under addition. In your setting, "linear space" just means module right? So there's always an addition, no?

Martin Winter said:

Actually one could replace SubMulAction₀ with SubMulAction in this case. Is there any reason left to introduce the former?

I remembered why we need SubMulAction₀: with SubMulAction the empty set would be a cone, while the intention (coming from homogenization) is to always have it contain 0.

Justus Springer said:

And I don't yet understand the motivation of adding a cone type that's not closed under addition. In your setting, "linear space" just means module right? So there's always an addition, no?

The motivation is to make linear and affine side work as similarly as possible, making (de)homogenization a "functor" between them. Currently they have a mismatch in what objects they bundle. Introducing non-convex cones on the linear side is one way to fix it.

When you homogenize a set in affine space, you get a SubMulAction₀ R≥0 M. If the latter don't exist, what is the natural object that can be dehomogenized? I guess we could use Set. Then dehomogenize-homogenize would act as a closure operation rather than an order isomoprhism. The closure operation is precisely closure under scalar multiplication (+ adding 0).
Do we ever homogenise an arbitrary set?
At least we may homogenize things more general than a convex set.

Martin Winter said:

Then dehomogenize-homogenize would act as a closure operation rather than an order isomoprhism.

So that would make them a docs#GaloisConnection. That doesn't sound like a bad way to set things up?
A docs#GaloisInsertion even (with l dehomogenisation and u homogenisation)

Justus Springer said:

So that would make them a docs#GaloisConnection. That doesn't sound like a bad way to set things up?

Maybe yeah. I will need to test how smooth this is in practice.

Martin Winter said:

Justus Springer said:

The distinction between cones with/without the origin seems very unnatural to me, so I would even be fine with dropping docs#ConvexCone in favor of docs#PointedCone.

Something like this has been on its way for a while, not sure about the status (Artie Khovanov).

It stalled out because someone said we might have uses for cones without the origin iirc

Martin Winter said:

By the way, I think the current ConvexCone can also be expressed as Submodule R>0 M if really needed.

It can't because the strictly positive elements don't form a semiring. Yaël asking for this generalisation of a semimodule is what started this whole discussion iirc.

Artie Khovanov said:

It stalled out because someone said we might have uses for cones without the origin iirc

But the name ConvexCone should be freed up independent of any such potential uses, right?

Yeah we could do a chained rename maybe
PointedCone -> ConvexCone
ConvexCone -> ?

Martin Winter said:

That is right! So perhaps we want to mirror the PointedCone setup and define

abbrev Cone (R M) := SubMulAction₀ R≥0 M

Actually one could replace SubMulAction₀ with SubMulAction in this case. Is there any reason left to introduce the former?

I would call this a "homogeneous set."

Artie Khovanov said:

It stalled out because someone said we might have uses for cones without the origin iirc

Do you mean here? My comments should not have stalled this.
We should be equally critical of keeping the bundle as we are for introduction a new one. In particular, I have not seen an application that would justifies a new bundle.

Artie Khovanov said:

I would call this a "homogeneous set."

Maybe HSet? A short name is preferred since we would coerce to it explicitly often. Or is a homogeneous set also for general rings, not only their nonneg semiring?
